mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% despite the tight labor market, indicating that the Fed will not feel compelled to tighten policy aggressively.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < -2%), it signals a supply chain disruption that will negatively impact corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The supply chain disruption is quickly resolved (e.g., due to targeted policy intervention) and industrial production rebounds within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed quickly reverses course and cuts rates due to financial instability or a sharp economic downturn, negating the restrictive impact on equities.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates (3-month change > 10%) and the unemployment rate is low (< 5%), it signals a strong consumer demand environment that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: A geopolitical shock or policy error causes a sudden drop in consumer confidence, negating the positive demand impulse.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < -100k) and the unemployment rate is already high (> 6%), it signals a rapidly weakening labor market that will depress consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Fiscal stimulus or other policy support quickly materializes to prop up the labor market and prevent a deeper downturn.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising and the CPI inflation rate is above 3%, it signals a high-inflation environment that will prompt aggressive Fed tightening and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed pivots to a more dovish stance due to financial instability or a sharp slowdown in growth, preventing the aggressive tightening needed to combat inflation.

mechanism_narrative: When real estate loans growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < -5%) and the housing starts growth is already negative (3-month change < -10%), it signals a rapidly weakening housing market that will depress consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month % change in RSAFS < -5% and 3-month % change in HOUST < -10%
failure_condition: The government announces a large-scale housing stimulus program that quickly reverses the decline in housing activity and supports consumer spending.
